subject: research/garment-optics
professional: a senior EMC / textile-shielding researcher refereeing for IEEE Transactions on Electromagnetic Compatibility or Textile Research Journal. They would check first whether the wire-mesh SE model is the accepted one (Casey 1988 / Kontorovich inductive-grid model, not a single-slot formula), whether the skin effect is handled at GHz, whether yarn breaks are allowed to enlarge apertures (not only raise Rs), whether the measurement literature (ASTM D4935 on metallised fabrics) is cited and compared, and whether the material constants are right

evidence.correctness: Everything the code computes reproduces and recomputes. `python3 experiments/run.py` in a scratch copy (2.9 s) writes results.txt byte-identical to the committed file; figure.py regenerates breakage.svg byte-identically. By hand from the textbook formulas: Ag 1 um on 100 um @1 mm gives R'=50.5 ohm/m, Rs=0.0505, sheet SE 71.4 dB, metal 6.59 g/m2 (all match results.txt); aperture at 2.4 GHz with g=0.95 mm is 36.36 dB (36.4); Rs for 30 dB is 6.151 (6.15). My own resistor-network solver (dense Laplacian pseudo-inverse with both bus bars contracted to single nodes, replaying the same break mask) agrees with effective_sheet_resistance to <1.3e-5 relative on four grids (n=10..20, f=0..0.4). EMT column equals Kirkpatrick (1973) bond-dilution EMT (p-pc)/(1-pc) with pc=1/2. Material constants check against handbook values (Cu 5.96e7, Ag 6.30e7, SS316 ~1.35e6 S/m; 8960/10490/8000 kg/m3). Not 4: the formulas are computed correctly but the combination (min of sheet and single-slot bound) is not the field's mesh model; that is scored under domain.
evidence.completeness: README promises 8 tests (`python3 -m pytest -q tests`: 8 passed in 0.35s), run.py 'seconds' (2.9 s, identical output), every Results bullet traceable to results.txt (all four checked: 6.2/1.9/0.19 ohm/sq; 54-87 dB sheet, 36.4/48-50/~15 dB aperture; 6.6 g/m2 36.8 dB, 2.6 g/m2 43.9 dB, 31-35 g/m2; 2.55 vs 2.50, 5.8 vs 5.0, 13/20 open at 0.5, 64.4->48.3 dB). Live page https://marisstella.app/research/garment-optics/ returns 200. The milestone's other three parts (structural colour, IR, adversarial patterns) are honestly listed as not done; the RF part it claims is complete.
evidence.verification: Tests pass (8). Seven seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 4 caught (mass factor 2->1 at model.py:59; rs_for_se /20->/10 at :53; wavelength halved at :42; break probability halved at :74), 3 survived: aperture gap p-d -> p in se_fabric (model.py:48, the function every SE number goes through), coating area halved (model.py:28, behind the silver-coated headline numbers), and SS316 conductivity x10 (model.py:21). Tests check formula identities and grid behaviour, never a design-level number or results.txt, and the coated-yarn path has no test at all.
evidence.craft: Read src/garment_optics/model.py (118 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py. Small, readable, src layout, sparse solve. Defects: `from ... import *` in tests and run.py; L[free] is re-sliced inside the bus-bar loop (model.py:94, O(n) slices of a CSR matrix); the 1e-12 leak to ground (model.py:97) is a silent regularisation that shifts results by ~1e-5; the figure's alt text says the curve rises 'to about 27 times ... by 50 percent' but figure.py:83 drops rows >= 0.5, so 27 is never plotted; the SE-vs-breakage table uses a fresh rng (run.py:44) so its 0.3 ratio (2.66) differs from the table above (2.548) for no stated reason. Nothing a reviewer would block.
evidence.claims: Disclosure is unusually good (no fabric measured, constants and citation from memory, AI assistance, min not validated, no prices). Two claims go further than the files: README.md:12 calls min(sheet, aperture) 'a conservative combination', and README.md:27 wonders whether the aperture bound is 'too pessimistic'; against the standard inductive wire-mesh model (Casey 1988) it is optimistic by about 6 dB at 1 mm pitch (30.2 vs 36.4 dB at 2.4 GHz, 9.4 vs 15.0 at 28 GHz; agrees within 1 dB at 0.3 mm). The bold conclusion 'modelled SE degrades gracefully until near the threshold' (README.md:29) is an artefact of letting breaks raise Rs only (run.py:47): a broken segment merges two openings into a ~2p slot, which by the README's own aperture formula costs ~6 dB as soon as breaks appear. Skin effect (Rac/Rdc ~9 for 50 um Cu at 2.4 GHz) is absent from Limitations.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can rerun it in 3 s and reuse the resistor-grid code, but the result is not new and partly unsound: the SE part applies two textbook formulas, the breakage part reproduces Kirkpatrick's 1973 EMT and the square-lattice bond threshold 1/2, and the nearest prior work on mesh and textile shielding (Casey 1988 IEEE Trans. EMC 30(3); Kontorovich's averaged boundary conditions; ASTM D4935 measurements of metallised fabrics) is not cited or compared. It does not reach research/CLAUDE.md's PhD-level, venue-aimed bar: one session, no measurement or published data point to calibrate against.
evidence.domain: Compared with EMC practice for wire meshes: a mesh is modelled as a sheet impedance Rs + j omega Ls with Ls = (mu0 p / 2 pi) ln(1/(1 - exp(-pi d/p))) (Casey), not as the min of a DC-resistance sheet and a single-slot lambda/2L bound; the single-slot formula also ignores the many-aperture penalty. DC resistance is used at GHz with no skin effect (fine for the 1 um Ag coatings, wrong by ~9x for solid Cu/Ag wire, though masked by the aperture term). Breaks change only Rs, never aperture size. Crossing contact resistance, which the README itself calls dominant, is not modelled. A referee would ask for the Casey model and one ASTM D4935 comparison before accepting any SE number.

defects.what: Fabric SE is min(DC thin-sheet SE, single-slot lambda/2g bound) rather than the standard wire-mesh sheet-impedance model (Casey 1988: Rs + j omega Ls). At 1 mm pitch the reported numbers are about 6 dB higher than Casey's (36.4 vs 30.2 dB at 2.4 GHz; 15.0 vs 9.4 at 28 GHz), so the headline SE figures for the 1 mm designs are optimistic, not conservative.

'Modelled SE degrades gracefully until near the threshold, then collapses' rests on breaks changing only Rs; a broken segment merges two openings into a ~2p slot, which by the model's own aperture formula costs ~6 dB as soon as breaks appear. The conclusion is an artefact of the modelling choice.
Tests never pin a design-level number or results.txt and the coated-yarn path is untested: aperture gap p-d -> p, coating area halved, and SS316 conductivity x10 all leave 8/8 green.
README calls the min combination 'conservative' and asks whether the aperture bound is 'too pessimistic'; against Casey's mesh model it is optimistic at 1 mm pitch.

Nearest prior work not cited: Casey (1988) wire-mesh shielding, Kirkpatrick (1973) for the EMT used, and measured metallised-fabric SE (ASTM D4935 studies); no published measurement to calibrate against.
DC resistance used at 0.9-28 GHz with no skin effect (Rac/Rdc ~9 for 50 um Cu at 2.4 GHz) and not listed in Limitations; masked today because the aperture term binds.
Figure alt text says the curve rises to about 27x by 50% breakage, but figure.py drops rows with f >= 0.5, so the plotted maximum is 5.8.

verdict: A small, honest, fully reproducible model: results.txt and the figure regenerate byte for byte in 3 s, five outputs recompute by hand or with my own resistor-network solver, and the disclosures (no fabric measured, constants and citation from memory, no prices) are better than most. It does not meet the bar. Verification is 2 (3 of 7 seeded mutants survive, including the aperture gap in the function every SE number goes through and the coated-yarn area behind the silver headline). Claims and domain are 2: the min(sheet, single-slot) combination called 'conservative' is about 6 dB optimistic at 1 mm pitch against Casey's (1988) standard wire-mesh model, skin effect is ignored, and the bold 'degrades gracefully' finding follows from letting breaks raise Rs but never enlarge apertures. As research it applies textbook formulas and reproduces Kirkpatrick's EMT without citing either, short of the PhD-level bar. Meets the bar: no (verification 2, claims 2, median 2).
